name: 6-Bid Solo
description: 6-Bid Solo: 3p trick-taking from German Tarok/Skat; popular in Salt Lake City. 36 cards; 11 each, 3-card widow. Bids: Solo (60+ pts), Heart Solo, Misère, Guarantee (74/80), Spread Misère, Call Solo (120). A-10-K-Q-J-9-8-7-6; 120 pts per round.

history.origins: Six-Bid Solo is an American three-player point-trick game in the German Ace-Ten tradition. It descends from the 36-card game Tappen (German Tarok), which was played in southern Germany, western Austria and Switzerland in the early 19th century and later gave rise to local American variants.
timeline: Modern Era: Continues to be played worldwide

setup.deck: 36 cards: A, 10, K, Q, J, 9, 8, 7, 6 in four suits (French). One standard 52-card deck with 2s, 3s, 4s, 5s removed.
setup.dealing: Deal a batch of 4 cards to each player, then 3 to each, then 3 cards face down in the center (widow), then 4 more to each. Eleven cards per player; the widow stays unseen until the end. Deal clockwise starting from the player to the dealer's left.
setup.equipment: 36-card deck, score sheet or chips for point settlement.

rules.objective: As declarer, meet your bid contract (e.g. take at least 61 card points in Solo, avoid all points in Misère, or take all 120 in Call Solo). As defenders, prevent the declarer from making the contract.
rules.gameplay: 1. Deal: 4-3-3 (widow)-4 to each of three players; widow stays face-down. 2. Bidding: Player to dealer's left bids first, then second; if both bid they alternate until one passes; then third player may bid. Bidding continues until one player remains. Six bids from lowest: Solo, Heart Solo, Misère, Guarantee Solo, Spread Misère, Call Solo. 3. Play: Declarer leads (except Spread Misère, where player to declarer's left leads and declarer's hand is spread face-up). Follow suit if possible; if not, play trump if able; no requirement to beat. Winner of trick leads next. 4. Scoring: Card points in tricks (and widow for declarer) determine success; each bid has a fixed score (30–150) paid to or by declarer.
keyRules: Must follow suit if possible; if void, must play trump if able.
61+ points wins for declarer in point bids; Misère = zero points; Guarantee = 74 (hearts) or 80 (other); Call Solo = all 120.

strategy.basic: Bid to your trump length; count tricks needed for contract.
strategy.intermediate: Solo vs partnership bids; defend by leading through declarer.
strategy.advanced: Six levels typical; trump choice and kitty use.
tips: Solo = one player against rest; bid levels reflect trick target.
